title: POC weekly sync — embeddings regression & hot-swap plan
next_steps: Redwood to run 1k-simulated-queries embedding regression suite and share results (csv)
Customer to provide 200 representative query prompts and expected relevance examples
Schedule lab test for hot-swap cutover during off-peak window (2 hours)
action_items: Diego Ramos - run embedding drift and centroid stability tests, attach metrics and logs - 2026-04-02
Tom Ridley - share prod sampling queries and vector-store config - 2026-04-01
Maria Chen - prepare hot-swap rollback playbook and safety checklist - 2026-04-03
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on recent embedding regression observed in search recall. Discussed candidate model pins, fallback/hot-swap strategy, and runbook for emergency cutover. Agreed Redwood will run a focused embedding regression suite and NovaCura will provide representative queries. Next: lab cutover test and share metrics for final pin decision.
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen: okay everyone thanks for hopping on, we wanted to focus this week on the embedding issues you flagged, and the hot-swap/rollback plan. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Elena Park: hi Elena, ML lead at NovaCura. we've seen drop in recall on the clinician search endpoint starting last thursday.
[00:18] Diego Ramos: sorry can you give a quick one-liner on the drop, like percent or what changed?
[00:22] Elena Park: yeah, roughly a 12–15% decline in top-5 MRR, across a sample of 5k queries. index hasn't changed, embeddings bucket was rolled last week to v2.1 and we think that's the culprit.
[00:35] Tom Ridley: to add, we also bumped the vector store config — we changed L2 normalization and the index snapshot is slightly different, but team suspects model mismatch.
[00:44] Maria Chen: got it. Diego, can you summarize what we saw in our quick triage?
[00:48] Diego Ramos: sure. we ran a blind comparison between v2.0 (pinned) and v2.1 (current) using a 500 sample. v2.1 had higher cosine variance and the centroids drifted ~0.07 on average which translated to nearest neighbor swaps. transcription note: centroid numbers are approximate, but you get the idea.
[01:10] Sofia Mendes: are those numbers stable across long queries? some of our clinical notes are long and were getting truncated during embedder tokenization, that could affect similarity.
[01:18] Priya Kumar: good point, we saw length sensitivity in v2.1 with longer documents leading to subtly different vector magnitudes. normalization setting in the store can mask but not fully correct it.
[01:30] Raj Patel: core question for us: do we pin back to v2.0 or switch to an alternative open model? also what's the hot-swap path with minimum downtime?
[01:38] Maria Chen: so two parallel threads — model decision (pin vs alternate) and operational plan (hot-swap + rollback). Diego, recommendations?
[01:44] Diego Ramos: for model decision, short-term safest is pin to v2.0 for search endpoints that need consistency. medium-term we should run a broader suite against 2k queries and evaluate embedding regressions, latency, and tokenization edge-cases. alternative models: there's a smaller quantized candidate that looks promising on recall but we need to test for hallucination and cost.
[02:05] Elena Park: cost is sensitive but consistency is higher priority. pinning is fine but we want a plan to surface degradation earlier.
[02:12] Maria Chen: agreed. on operational side, our hot-swap plan is: deploy new embedding model to shadow mode, warm the cache, run a scoring pass, then do a staged cutover with traffic split (80/20, 50/50) and a fail-open back to pinned model. we can automate rollback if top-N recall falls below threshold.
[02:32] Tom Ridley: what threshold would trigger auto-rollback?
[02:34] Diego Ramos: suggestion: if top-5 MRR drops >5% over a rolling 1hr vs baseline, trigger rollback. but we can tune to customer tolerance.
[02:45] Sofia Mendes: will that detect subtle semantics regressions? some of our queries are rare, they may not show up in a rolling 1hr window.
[02:52] Priya Kumar: we recommend both rolling metrics and periodic probe queries — a small set of golden queries that run constantly to detect regressions; those are weighted higher in the decision.
[03:03] Raj Patel: ok, actionably, we need Diego's regression suite and a golden queries set. Tom will supply representative queries.
[03:10] Maria Chen: timeline check — Diego can you run the 1k and 2k suites and share result csv by Friday?
[03:15] Diego Ramos: yes, target end-of-day Friday. note: we'll include centroid drift, cosine variance, recall delta, and latency per embed call.
[03:25] Elena Park: also please include tokenization mismatches — sometimes clinical shorthand exploded tokens.
[03:30] Diego Ramos: will do.
[03:32] Tom Ridley: on hot-swap, do you support atomic swap for vector snapshots? we can't afford partial index inconsistencies.
[03:39] Priya Kumar: Redwood supports index warm-up and atomic swap for our managed vector caching layer in Dedicated; for Private customers we provide the playbook and a script to perform snapshot swap. minor transcription glitch: 'atomic' sounded like 'a tonic' earlier in our notes.
[03:53] Maria Chen: good to call out. recovery playbook will have pre-checks: snapshot integrity, checksum, warm-up traffic, health probes, and a fallback window.
[04:03] Sofia Mendes: what's the expected downtime for a hot-swap cutover if we do a full swap?
[04:07] Diego Ramos: if everything is warmed and the index swap is atomic, downtime is typically sub-30 seconds for redirecting traffic; the bigger risk is semantic regression, not connectivity.
[04:16] Raj Patel: competitors question — we tried Pinecone's quick-swap last year and it was fast but we lost some nearest-neighbor stability. how does Redwood's approach differ?
[04:24] Diego Ramos: Pinecone tends to re-hash on rebuild, which can change neighbor distances; our approach emphasizes warm-up and gradual routing plus centroids drift monitoring so you can detect stability early.
[04:36] Elena Park: are there metrics we should look at besides MRR? precision@k, recall@k, mean reciprocal rank, and some embedding distance distribution metrics?
[04:45] Diego Ramos: yes include precision@5, recall@10, mean rank, and average cosine variance. we'll also surface per-query deltas for golden probes.
[04:55] Tom Ridley: just flag: our compliance team needs an audit trail of any hot-swap. can you include that in the playbook?
[05:02] Maria Chen: yes, we'll include audit-log steps, signatures, and KMS key references for Private deployment.
[05:09] Elena Park: ok timeline recap?
[05:11] Maria Chen: Diego runs suites by Friday; Tom shares queries by Thursday; Maria drafts playbook by next Monday and we'll schedule a 2-hour lab cutover next week during off-peak.
[05:22] Raj Patel: sounds good. any other open risks?
[05:24] Priya Kumar: data residency wasn't an issue here, but for completeness, if you decide to use a hosted fallback in a different region we need to be careful about PII and residency rules.
[05:34] Elena Park: noted.\n[05:37] Maria Chen: great — we'll follow up in the thread with links to the regression suite and a small spreadsheet for golden probes. thanks everyone, we'll close out.
[05:46] Tom Ridley: thanks.
[05:47] Sofia Mendes: bye.
[05:48] (call ends)
